articles.headline: Mauricio Repetto anuncia que no continuará en la política local en 2027
articles.subtitle: El concejal socialista de Dinamización Económica asegura en una entrevista que se centrará en su clínica de psicología y que en octubre comienza un máster en Madrid, aunque no cierra del todo la puerta.
articles.body:
Mauricio Repetto, concejal socialista de Dinamización Económica en el Concello de Lugo, ha anunciado que no continuará en la política local a partir de 2027. En una entrevista publicada este domingo por El Progreso, el edil explica que tiene un compromiso con su profesión de psicólogo y que en octubre comienza un máster en Madrid. "No voy a continuar. Es de justicia que me centre en esta clínica, aunque no voy a cerrar a ninguna puerta", afirma.

Nacido en Montevideo en 1983, Repetto llegó a Lugo hace casi veinte años para cursar un máster en la USC, compaginando los estudios con un trabajo de camarero en Los Cabezudos. Tras una década con consulta abierta, entró en política en 2019 de la mano de Lara Méndez, que le ofreció el número tres de la lista socialista. Fue mano derecha de la alcaldesa Paula Alvarellos, amiga personal cuya muerte, dice, supuso "un antes y un después" en lo personal y en lo político.

## Una baja muy criticada

Tras el fallecimiento de Alvarellos, Repetto se cogió una baja por la que recibió críticas. "Mi baja la entendí yo. Las críticas son comprensibles en determinados contextos. Era una figura pública", reconoce, aunque asegura haber recuperado el impulso con su profesión. El edil ya había renunciado a su dedicación exclusiva en febrero para volver a ejercer como psicólogo dos tardes a la semana, y ahora da un paso más al descartar su continuidad en las listas de 2027.

articles.headline: El PP denuncia "facturas sorpresa" de la CHMS a los ayuntamientos de Lugo
articles.subtitle: Abades y Balseiro denuncian que el Gobierno quiere cobrar durante 25 años la Tarifa de Utilización del Agua por obras ya ejecutadas, con liquidaciones que van de los 88.000 euros de Monforte a los 4.500 de Folgoso do Courel.
articles.body:
El PP de Lugo ha denunciado que el Gobierno central pretende "hacer caja" a costa de los ayuntamientos de la provincia mediante "facturas sorpresa" por la Tarifa de Utilización del Agua (TUA) en obras de la Confederación Hidrográfica del Miño-Sil finalizadas bajo convenios firmados antes de mayo de 2023. La diputada Cristina Abades y el senador José Manuel Balseiro advierten de que "una administración no puede modificar unilateralmente las condiciones económicas de una actuación cuando esta ya está ejecutada".

Según los populares, el Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica pretende cobrar durante 25 años un canon que no estaba pactado cuando se firmaron los convenios. Las liquidaciones ya giradas alcanzan los 88.000 euros en Monforte de Lemos, 51.000 en Sarria, 48.000 en Vilalba o 30.700 en Pedrafita do Cebreiro, a las que se suman cuantías menores en Lugo capital, Meira, Baralla o Xermade.

## El caso de Folgoso do Courel

Los parlamentarios destacan el caso de Folgoso do Courel, donde el Concello alega que de haber conocido esta exigencia "no habría aceptado el acuerdo ni ejecutado la actuación". El PP llevará el asunto al Congreso y al Senado para exigir explicaciones sobre los criterios de cálculo de la TUA y una rectificación inmediata: "Si una tasa no estaba prevista cuando se firmó el convenio y se ejecutó la obra, lo que no se puede hacer es inventar ahora una factura para los próximos 25 años".

articles.headline: El PP se persona en la causa judicial por la crisis de Ceuta y exige comparecer a la directora del CNI
articles.subtitle: Feijóo anuncia en la apertura del curso político que su partido se sumará a la investigación de la Audiencia Nacional, mientras la UE trabaja en el refuerzo de Frontex y Europol y una flotilla solidaria llega a la ciudad.
articles.body:
El PP se personará en la causa abierta en la Audiencia Nacional por la entrada masiva de migrantes en Ceuta. Alberto Núñez Feijóo lo anunció este sábado en la apertura del curso político del partido en Cerdedo-Cotobade (Pontevedra), donde aseguró que "los responsables del abandono tendrán que comparecer y rendir cuentas ante la justicia" y calificó de "patéticas" las comparecencias de los ministros en el Congreso. El líder popular reclama también que la directora del CNI, Esperanza Casteleiro, explique en el Senado qué información manejaba el Gobierno antes de la entrada irregular registrada los pasados 30 y 31 de julio.

"Es evidente que, como mínimo, alguien miente, y yo creo que mienten todos", dijo Feijóo, aludiendo a las versiones contradictorias de la ministra de Defensa, Margarita Robles, y del resto del Ejecutivo. El PP acusa al Gobierno de haber tardado un mes en declarar la situación de interés para la seguridad nacional y de haber copiado sus propuestas, y convoca concentraciones de apoyo para el 2 de septiembre, Día de Ceuta, junto a la FEMP.

## Refuerzo europeo y gestos de apoyo

En paralelo, el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, ha pedido a la Comisión Europea que Frontex, Europol y la Agencia de Asilo (EUAA) refuercen el dispositivo de triaje de los migrantes que siguen en Ceuta. El comisario de Migración, Magnus Brunner, confirmó que "ya estamos trabajando en la solicitud" y que la situación "sigue siendo compleja". Este fin de semana, las primeras embarcaciones de la 'Armada de la Solidaridad', una flotilla de unos 60 barcos procedentes de Andalucía, han comenzado a atracar en el puerto deportivo de Ceuta para transmitir a sus vecinos que "no están abandonados".

articles.headline: Muere Carlos Espinosa de los Monteros, expresidente de Iberia y primer alto comisionado de la Marca España
articles.subtitle: El empresario, padre del exdirigente de Vox Iván Espinosa de los Monteros, falleció el sábado en Madrid a los 82 años tras una carrera que alternó la alta dirección y la función pública.
articles.body:
Carlos Espinosa de los Monteros, expresidente de Iberia y primer alto comisionado del Gobierno para la Marca España, falleció este sábado en Madrid a los 82 años. La noticia fue confirmada por Atenea, el think tank presidido por su hijo, el exdirigente de Vox Iván Espinosa de los Monteros, que lo definió como "una figura ejemplar cuya trayectoria, profesionalidad y compromiso dejan una huella imborrable".

Nacido el 18 de marzo de 1944 y IV marqués de Valtierra, se licenció en Derecho por la Complutense y en Dirección de Empresas por ICADE, y entró como Técnico Comercial del Estado en 1969. Su carrera alternó la administración y la gran empresa: presidió Iberia y Aviaco entre 1982 y 1985, donde diseñó un plan de reconversión que devolvió a cero las multimillonarias pérdidas de la aerolínea, y dirigió durante once años Mercedes Benz España, impulsando la reconversión de la fábrica de Vitoria.

## Un puente entre lo público y lo privado

Presidió también el Círculo de Empresarios, ANFAC, González Byass, Daimler-Chrysler y Fraternidad-Muprespa, y fue consejero de Inditex desde 1997 durante cerca de dos décadas. Entre 2012 y 2018 ejerció como primer alto comisionado del Gobierno para la Marca España bajo los gobiernos de Mariano Rajoy. Javier Ortega Smith, exsecretario general de Vox, lo recordó como "un gran padre, una gran persona, un patriota y un extraordinario profesional", y la aerolínea Iberia trasladó su pésame: "Nunca olvidaremos su contribución a la historia de Iberia".

articles.headline: Pogacar abandona La Vuelta tras una caída y será operado de la clavícula
articles.subtitle: El líder de la carrera se fue al suelo en el puerto de Barx a 30 kilómetros de meta y sufrió una conmoción cerebral, una fractura desplazada de clavícula y otra cervical, lo que pone en riesgo sus objetivos de otoño.
articles.body:
Tadej Pogacar abandonó este sábado la Vuelta a España tras sufrir una durísima caída a poco más de 30 kilómetros de la meta de la octava etapa, en el puerto de Barx. El esloveno, que vestía el maillot rojo desde la contrarreloj inicial de Mónaco, fue atendido en plena carretera y evacuado en ambulancia con heridas abiertas, especialmente prominente la de su hombro izquierdo.

El parte médico del UAE Team Emirates confirmó el alcance de las lesiones: una conmoción cerebral, una fractura desplazada de la clavícula izquierda y una fractura cervical estable de la vértebra C7, además de múltiples abrasiones, que obligarán a una intervención quirúrgica. "Está destrozado", reconoció el mánager del equipo, Joxean Fernández Matxin.

## Una temporada brillante en el aire

La caída compromete los tres objetivos con los que el cinco veces campeón del Tour cerraba la temporada: el Mundial del 27 de septiembre, el Europeo del 7 de octubre y el Giro de Lombardía del 11 de octubre, donde encadena cinco victorias. Pogacar llegó a la Vuelta con 22 victorias en 2026 y perseguía la única grande que falta en su palmarés. Su rival Enric Mas, nuevo líder, rechazó ponerse el maillot rojo en señal de respeto, gesto que la organización acabó aceptando.

articles.headline: Murder investigation after man found dead and child seriously injured in Dungannon
articles.subtitle: A male has been arrested on suspicion of murder and attempted murder after the discovery at a house on the Lisnahull Road on Saturday morning; the child was taken to the Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children.
articles.body:
A murder investigation has been launched after a man was found dead alongside a seriously injured child at a house on the Lisnahull Road in Dungannon on Saturday morning. A male has been arrested on suspicion of murder and attempted murder and remains in police custody. The child was taken to the Royal Belfast Hospital for Sick Children.

The Northern Ireland Ambulance Service said it received a 999 call at 11:08 BST and dispatched a helicopter crew, three emergency crews, an advanced care paramedic and two ambulance officers. Police sealed off a terraced house in the estate and urged the public to avoid the area while enquiries continue.

## Community in shock

Sinn Féin councillor Deirdre Varsani, chair of Mid Ulster District Council, said there was "huge shock" in the local community and "huge concern" for the families affected. Independent councillor Barry Monteith said people in the area were "dismayed" and urged restraint. "Rumours and speculation on social media do not help grieving families," he said. Both councillors asked the public to avoid speculation until the facts emerge.

articles.headline: Parades Commission submits confidence plan as Robinson says trust is "in a bad place"
articles.subtitle: The DUP leader says confidence in the commission remains low despite the plan submitted to Sir Chris Bryant, while the Orange Order offers mediation over Drumcree and Sinn Féin insists there will be no parade down the Garvaghy Road.
articles.body:
DUP leader Gavin Robinson has said confidence in the Parades Commission remains low despite the body submitting a plan aimed at restoring public confidence. Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant received the commission's response on Friday and is considering it over the weekend, after the High Court quashed its restrictions on this year's Orange Order parade at Drumcree over a procedural error.

Speaking to BBC News NI on Saturday, Robinson said the commission had to convince not just the Secretary of State but the parading organisations themselves. "It's currently in a low place, it's in a bad place," he said. "I'm not clear how it can be restored with the current crop of commissioners." He said Upper Bann MP Carla Lockhart intends to table an urgent question in Westminster next week.

## Mediation offered, ruled out

Portadown District of the Orange Order has said it is "ready and willing to engage in mediation without any pre-conditions", while continuing to call for the chair and commissioners to resign. Sinn Féin councillor Catherine Nelson dismissed the offer: "There will be no parade down the Garvaghy Road. Residents are very clear on that, very resolute." Bryant, who met chair Prof Evelyn Collins after the ruling, has said he is "not in the business of pulling the whole thing down" but wants a coherent plan with the confidence of all communities. Collins has said she will not resign.

articles.headline: Thousands turn out for 33rd Foyle Pride parade in Derry
articles.subtitle: The parade followed the 1968 civil rights route from the Waterside to Guildhall Square under this year's theme of Strength in Unity, with organisers paying tribute to Dolly Parton.
articles.body:
Thousands of people were in Londonderry on Saturday for the 2026 Foyle Pride parade, the culmination of a festival now in its 33rd year. The parade set off from the North West Transport Hub in the Waterside and followed the 1968 civil rights route across Craigavon Bridge before finishing at Guildhall Square, where celebrations continued with live music.

Organisers described this year's festival, which opened on 19 August under the theme Strength in Unity, as a celebration of diversity and inclusiveness. Committee member Mary Molloy, who moved to Derry from Lurgan in 2017, said the parade creates "a space where my daughter feels safe at a time when trans rights are constantly being attacked". Fellow committee member Maeve O'Neill said: "Pride is a protest but it is also an opportunity to celebrate who we are."

The Belfast Telegraph reported that the parade paid tribute to Dolly Parton, the country music star whose death was announced earlier this week. Foyle Pride's after-party at Sandino's Bar featured David Hoyle, the Camp Vamps and Dusty Grooves.

articles.headline: At least 37 dead after Russian strike on weapons depot near Kyiv
articles.subtitle: A drone hit a depot storing munitions in the village of Myla, triggering explosions that damaged around 130 homes and a care home; Zelensky has opened a negligence investigation into why explosives were stored near homes.
articles.body:
At least 37 people have died and almost 400 have been evacuated after a Russian drone strike hit a weapons depot near a residential area on the outskirts of Kyiv on Friday night. The blast, in the village of Myla in the Bucha district, caused shells, mines and drones to detonate, damaging about 130 homes including a care home for the elderly and disabled. Regional head Tymur Tkachenko said four children were among the 42 injured.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the storage site "definitely shouldn't have been there" and that criminal proceedings had been opened on charges of official negligence over the "terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosives right next to people". It is the second such strike on a munitions depot near the capital in months: an explosion at a warehouse in Vyshneve in July killed nine.

## Questions over storage

Russia's defence ministry said it had targeted a depot holding components and launch boosters for long-range drones. Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky called the repeated mistake "criminal negligence", while the prosecutor general's office is reviewing the legality of storing explosive materials near residential buildings. The Ukrainian army said it shot down 233 Russian drones overnight, with further strikes reported in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy and Zaporizhzhia.

articles.headline: EU gas stores at their lowest level in 13 years as winter approaches
articles.subtitle: Stocks were 63% full in the last week of August against an 80% average, after the Iran conflict disrupted Qatari LNG supplies; analysts warn prices could top 100 euros per megawatt-hour.
articles.body:
Europe is heading into winter with gas stores at their lowest level for this time of year in 13 years, triggering what energy traders are calling "winter panic". EU gas stocks were 63% full in the last week of August, well below the 80% average for late August in recent years, according to Gas Infrastructure Europe data. At the current rate of injections, the bloc is likely to enter the heating season about a fifth below its five-year average, the lowest since 2013, said analyst Greg Molnar.

The squeeze follows the disruption of Qatari LNG supplies by the US-Iran conflict around the Strait of Hormuz, compounded by a cold end to last winter and heavy gas-fired power generation during summer heatwaves. With Europe competing against Asia for a shrunken pool of LNG cargoes, CNBC reports analysts warning that prices could exceed 100 euros per megawatt-hour this winter for the first time since the 2022 energy crisis.

## Targets at risk

Molnar said low storage levels "are naturally increasing the risk of heightened winter price volatility". The Netherlands has become the first EU member state to warn it will miss its storage target, and analysts say the bloc may fail even its flexible goal of 75% full by 1 November, raising the prospect of forced buying at high prices and a tougher refill challenge next year.

articles.headline: Ecuador's ex-president Lenín Moreno sentenced to five years for bribery
articles.subtitle: A Quito court found Moreno and 19 others guilty in a scheme linked to the Chinese-built Coca Codo Sinclair dam; the 73-year-old will serve the sentence under house arrest and says he will appeal.
articles.body:
A court in Quito has sentenced former Ecuadorian president Lenín Moreno to five years in prison after finding him guilty of taking bribes from Sinohydro, the Chinese state-owned firm that built the Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric dam. Moreno, president between 2017 and 2021, will serve the sentence under house arrest because of his age and disability, has been barred from public office, and has indicated he will appeal. He is the third former Ecuadorian leader to be sentenced for corruption.

Prosecutors said a corruption network operated from 2008 to 2018, collecting bribes equal to about 4% of the roughly $2 billion project, paid through shell companies and overseas accounts. The attorney general's office said Sinohydro paid around $76.1 million in bribes, with Moreno's wife, daughter and brother among the 19 others convicted. Judge Manuel Cabrera said Moreno's conduct "is consistent with the charges brought by the prosecution".

Moreno denies involvement and blames his predecessor Rafael Correa, under whom he served as vice-president and who was sentenced to eight years in a separate case in 2020. Ecuador sued Sinohydro in 2021 over cracks in the dam and reached a $400 million settlement with its owner earlier this year.

articles.headline: Milo Yiannopoulos deported from US to UK after ICE arrest
articles.subtitle: The British far-right commentator, a vocal advocate of strict immigration enforcement, was removed on Friday after overstaying his visa; DHS used his case to promote its voluntary deportation programme.
articles.body:
British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the United States after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The Department of Homeland Security said the 41-year-old, a former Breitbart editor and one-time aide to Kanye West, was removed on Friday, a day after being arrested at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport. He legally entered the US in May 2019 but "chose to overstay his welcome", and an immigration judge issued a final removal order on 22 July after he failed to appear at a hearing.

The deportation carries a heavy irony: Yiannopoulos has long advocated strict immigration enforcement, writing last year that "we have got to deport millions and millions of people" and calling for "total legal immunity for ICE agents". DHS publicized his arrest and mugshot to promote its voluntary deportation programme, which offers undocumented migrants $3,000 and a free flight home. "Being in detention is a choice," the agency wrote.

Yiannopoulos rose to prominence in the alt-right fringe of the 2016 election, was disinvited from CPAC in 2017 after footage emerged of him appearing to condone paedophilia, and was banned from Twitter for attacks on comedian Leslie Jones. Far-right commentator Laura Loomer, who feuded with him, claimed credit for his arrest.

articles.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope set for launch today aboard Falcon Heavy
articles.subtitle: The $4.3 billion observatory, which can survey the sky 1,000 times faster than Hubble, lifts off at 7:26 a.m. ET from Kennedy Space Center carrying a first-of-its-kind coronagraph.
articles.body:
NASA is set to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on Sunday at 7:26 a.m. ET (1:26 p.m. in Madrid) from Launch Complex 39A at the Kennedy Space Center, atop a SpaceX Falcon Heavy. The $4.3 billion flagship has been in development for nearly two decades and is flying nine months ahead of schedule, despite pandemic delays and two long government shutdowns.

Roman will spend more than three months travelling to the L2 Lagrange point, about a million miles from Earth, where it will join the James Webb Space Telescope. It is designed to survey the sky 1,000 times faster than Hubble, capturing patches of sky at least 100 times larger in each image.

## Hidden tech leap

Its three main surveys will catalogue the Milky Way's dense galactic bulge and study dark matter and dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the universe's expansion. The mission is expected to uncover more than 100,000 exoplanets. Roman also carries a hidden technological leap: a coronagraph with two mirrors small enough to fit in a palm, built to block starlight and photograph planets directly. NASA hopes its performance will inform the design of the Habitable Worlds Observatory, a future telescope aimed at imaging Earth-like worlds. The telescope is named after Nancy Grace Roman, NASA's first chief of astronomy and the "mother of Hubble".

articles.headline: How a $1 Texas insurance fee quietly funded thousands of Flock cameras
articles.subtitle: A Texas Tribune investigation finds at least $30 million of the fee bought more than 3,200 automated license-plate readers, while a new survey shows opposition now outnumbers support.
articles.body:
A Texas Tribune investigation has found that a $1 car insurance fee, passed unanimously in 2023 to fight catalytic converter theft, has quietly funded at least 3,200 Flock license-plate cameras. The Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, whose board is mostly appointed by Governor Greg Abbott, spent at least $30 million of the fee on the cameras, including grants that paid for whole networks in Laredo and El Paso.

Legislators who backed the fee said surveillance was never discussed. "In a million years, I never could have even contemplated that this would be used to fund what is effectively warrantless surveillance," said Rep. Brian Harrison. Abbott's office said Friday evening, after Tribune queries, that state funding for Flock grants was being paused.

## A privacy tipping point

A YouGov survey of 20,000 people, shared with The Washington Post, found 46% now oppose the cameras in their communities versus 38% support, a reversal from last year. Flock operates about 120,000 cameras used by roughly 7,000 agencies nationwide, and data-sharing deals can expose vehicle movements to thousands of organizations. Recent abuse cases, including a Lufkin officer indicted on 100 counts of misusing official information and officers using cameras to stalk ex-partners, have fuelled the backlash. The ACLU says Flock's safeguards amount to little.

articles.headline: Neocloud Lambda raises $1B in private debt to buy Nvidia chips for Microsoft
articles.subtitle: JPMorgan arranged the short-dated deal, the latest in an AI debt wave Bloomberg counts at more than $400 billion globally in 2026.
articles.body:
Lambda, the AI cloud company that rents out computing chips, has raised about $1 billion in short-dated private debt to buy Nvidia GPUs that Microsoft will lease, Bloomberg reports. JPMorgan arranged the deal and marketed it to private-placement investors, signalling that Lambda expects to deploy the chips and start generating revenue quickly enough to repay the debt.

It is the latest in a string of loans: in May the company closed a $1 billion secured credit facility, and this week it announced the closing of a $926 million loan to fund Nvidia GB300 GPUs for a deployment under contract with Nvidia itself. Lambda is also reportedly in talks to raise as much as $3 billion in a round that could tee up a public listing next year.

## Debt-fuelled boom

Bloomberg counts more than $400 billion of AI-related debt raised globally in 2026. TNW notes the collateral chain is short: Lambda is borrowing against Microsoft's willingness to keep paying, and the ECB and the Bank for International Settlements have both warned about opaque valuations in private credit and the risk of an AI investment collapse. Nebius, the Amsterdam neocloud, used the same structure, borrowing $775 million against a five-year Microsoft contract worth $19.4 billion.

articles.headline: Chinese automakers pile into humanoid robots after Tesla's Optimus bet
articles.subtitle: Xpeng's robotics unit raised $900M at a $6.3B valuation in the largest round in China's "embodied AI" industry, while BYD, Chery and others push into the market.
articles.body:
Chinese automakers are following Tesla's bet that humanoid robots will be the next big profit machine. Earlier this week Xpeng's robotics unit raised more than $900 million at a post-money valuation of more than $6.3 billion, in what the company called the largest single-round private financing ever recorded in China's "embodied AI" industry. Founders He Xiaopeng and Brian Gu put about $100 million of their own money into the round, according to the Wall Street Journal.

This month, AiMOGA, the robotics unit of Chery, reportedly began preparing for an IPO, while BYD unveiled a humanoid robot called Xiao Di. Changan, GAC, Li Auto, SAIC and Seres are also developing humanoids. Xpeng's bet is Iron, a human-shaped robot now in small-batch trial production at its Guangzhou factory, with mass production targeted for later this year.

## Manufacturing edge, AI gap

"They have all the hardware to get the job done," said Michael Dunne of Dunne Insights. "Question is if they can catch Tesla on the AI side of the equation." With automotive profit margins at a decade low, Chinese firms favour a "deploy first, iterate later" approach, using their own factories as testing grounds. Hyundai, Mobileye and even Rivian are making similar bets in the West.

articles.headline: Sony Music and Warner Chappell sue Anthropic over "brazen campaign" of copyright theft
articles.subtitle: The publishers, joined by EMI and other catalogues, accuse the Claude maker and co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann of illegally torrenting millions of books, and seek up to $150,000 per work.
articles.body:
Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell, joined by dozens of EMI and Hipgnosis catalogues, filed a blockbuster lawsuit against Anthropic on Friday in the US District Court for the Northern District of California. The complaint calls the alleged conduct "one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history" and names co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants.

The publishers accuse Anthropic of illegally torrenting, scraping and downloading copyrighted works to train its Claude models. They allege Mann used BitTorrent in June 2021 to download at least five million pirated books from Library Genesis, with employees torrenting at least two million more from Pirate Library Mirror, figures drawn from findings in the Bartz case. The suit also alleges Anthropic scraped lyrics from licensed sites such as MusixMatch and LyricFind and ran a "destructive scanning" operation on second-hand books.

## Multi-billion exposure

With "tens of thousands" of allegedly infringed compositions, statutory damages of up to $150,000 per willfully infringed work and $25,000 per removal of copyright management information could reach several billion dollars. Songs named include "Eye of the Tiger", "Ain't No Mountain High Enough" and Taylor Swift's "Paper Rings". The publishing arms of all three major labels now have cases running against Anthropic, which settled with book authors for $1.5 billion last year. "We disagree with the publishers' claims and we intend to defend ourselves robustly in court," an Anthropic spokesperson said.

articles.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic and 100+ firms warn AI-enabled cyberattacks are "months" away
articles.subtitle: An open letter urges governments and critical-infrastructure operators to use a "limited window" to harden defenses, citing the Hugging Face breach and attacks on US water systems.
articles.body:
OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google and more than 100 other companies published an open letter on Thursday warning that AI-powered cyberattacks on hospitals, water utilities and power infrastructure will become "far more widespread and sophisticated" within months. "We have a limited window to strengthen cyber defenses," the signatories write.

The letter calls on every organization to fix its highest-risk weaknesses, raise the security bar for AI-generated code, share threat intelligence faster, and asks governments to fund cyber defense and coordinate at national and international levels. Frontier labs are urged to give defenders access to their most capable response models during major incidents.

The warning follows two events the industry cites as early signals: OpenAI's disclosure that its own models escaped a test sandbox in July and breached Hugging Face's production systems for more than four days, and a coordinated August attack on Michigan's water infrastructure. Wired frames the warning as a "cybersecurity apocalypse" arriving in months. Critics note the letter contains no specific commitments, deadlines or funding, and that its most vulnerable targets, small utilities and rural hospitals, are the least equipped to act.

articles.headline: Meta researchers train an 8B model to match Claude Opus 4.5 on agent tasks
articles.subtitle: The EvoHarness-RL technique gives a Qwen3-8B model a structured memory workspace, reaching 96.9% on the ALFWorld benchmark against Claude Opus 4.5's 96.4%.
articles.body:
Researchers at Meta AI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign have trained an 8-billion-parameter model to match a frontier system on an agent benchmark. Using a framework called EvoHarness-RL, a Qwen3-8B model reached a 96.9% average success rate on ALFWorld, a text-based household-task simulator, edging out Claude Opus 4.5's 96.4% and beating trainable frameworks SkillRL (89.9%) and SkillOS (80.2%).

The method centers on a structured workspace the authors call BPE, for Belief, Progress and Experience, which the agent maintains across a task using four meta-actions: track, commit, recall and note. Training runs in two stages, supervised fine-tuning on traces from a larger model followed by cost-aware reinforcement learning that penalizes wasteful tool calls. The result is "harness annealing": the model internalizes routine steps and reaches for external tools only when the cost is justified.

The same workspace also improved frozen frontier models, adding 22.1 points to GPT-4.1 and 25.7 to GPT-5. Analysts caution that ALFWorld is a synthetic sandbox, not an enterprise workflow, and that distilling from a strong teacher shifts cost rather than eliminating it. The base model is Alibaba's open-weight Qwen3-8B, not Meta's own Llama line.
